questions.cardDe: Durch welche Stadt fließt die Donau nicht: Belgrad, Straßburg oder Wien?
questions.de: Straßburg liegt nicht an der Donau. An welchem großen Strom liegt die Stadt?
questions.en: Strasbourg does not lie on the Danube. Which great river does the city lie on?

timeline.labelDe: Der römische Feldherr Drusus gründet Straßburg (Argentoratum)

questions.notes: Card asks which of Belgrade, Strasbourg, Vienna is NOT on the Danube (Strasbourg); reworked to the positive fact. Its eastern districts and port border the Rhine, opposite Kehl.

questions.cardDe: Der erste Mensch, dessen Name 3.000 v. Chr. schriftlich festgehalten wurde, war was von Beruf: Krieger, Autor oder Buchhalter?
questions.de: Kuschim gilt als der erste Mensch, dessen Name schriftlich festgehalten wurde. Welches Getreide verbuchte er laut den Tontafeln aus Uruk?
questions.en: Kushim is considered the first person whose name was recorded in writing. Which grain did he keep accounts of, according to the clay tablets from Uruk?

timeline.labelEn: Uruk-period clay tablets naming Kushim, the earliest known personal name in writing
timeline.labelDe: Tontafeln der Uruk-Zeit mit dem Namen Kuschim, dem ältesten schriftlich überlieferten Personennamen

questions.notes: Multiple choice removed; the card's answer is 'Buchhalter' (accountant). Wikipedia: Kushim (fl. c. 3200 BC) appears on Uruk-period tablets recording barley transactions and 'was responsible for the production and storage of barley'; it is uncertain whether the name is an individual, an office title or an institution.

questions.cardDe: Als was verwendeten Tiroler Maler im Österreich des 18. Jahrhunderts Spinnweben: Pinsel, Leinwand oder Bilderrahmen?
questions.de: Als was verwendeten Tiroler Maler im Österreich des 18. Jahrhunderts Spinnweben?
questions.en: What did Tyrolean painters in 18th-century Austria use cobwebs as?

timeline.labelEn: Cobweb painting flourishes in (South) Tyrol, 18th to early 19th century
timeline.labelDe: Blüte der Spinnwebmalerei in (Süd-)Tirol, 18. bis frühes 19. Jahrhundert

questions.notes: Options removed. Cobweb (gossamer) painting: painting on canvases made from collected, layered spider and caterpillar webs, practised mainly in South Tyrol in the 18th and early 19th centuries; fewer than 100 survive.

questions.de: Vögel haben Nasenlöcher. Welcher Vogel trägt sie als einziger am Ende seines langen Schnabels?
questions.en: Birds do have nostrils. Which bird is the only one with its nostrils at the end of its long beak?

timeline.labelEn: George Shaw names the kiwi genus Apteryx
timeline.labelDe: George Shaw benennt die Kiwi-Gattung Apteryx

questions.notes: Card statement is false (birds have nostrils); reworked to an open question on bird nostrils. Kiwi 'are the only birds with nostrils at the end of their long beaks' and use them to smell prey.

questions.cardDe: Wie viele Tennisbälle werden jährlich für die Wimbledon-Turniere bestellt: über 10.000, 30.000 oder 50.000?
questions.de: Wie viele Tennisbälle werden jährlich für die Wimbledon-Turniere bestellt?
questions.en: How many tennis balls are ordered each year for the Wimbledon Championships?

timeline.labelEn: Slazenger begins supplying the balls for Wimbledon
timeline.labelDe: Slazenger liefert erstmals die Bälle für Wimbledon

source.title: Facts and Figures / FAQ – The Championships, Wimbledon (archived)

questions.notes: Options removed. Official Wimbledon facts page: '54,250 used during The Championships’ period'; other reports give about 54,000–55,000 per year, so accept any answer of roughly 50,000–55,000. Slazenger has supplied the balls since 1902 (en.wikipedia Wimbledon Championships).
